original_assignment_row.title: Agricultural Sector Devastated: China Soybean Exports Collapse 72%, $14.9B Loss
original_assignment_row.description_short: Agricultural Sector Devastated: China Soybean Exports Collapse 72%, $14.9B Loss
original_assignment_row.description_medium: Reuters reported in August 2025 that U.S. soybean sales to China were losing ground during a key supply period as Brazilian exports filled demand. The linked report does not substantiate the assignment’s full-year 2025 agricultural export totals, the $14.9 billion estimate or the claimed 72% soybean decline. original_assignment_row.description_long: China's retaliatory tariffs in 2025 reduced U.S. agricultural exports to China from $24.5 billion in 2024 to just $8.4 billion in 2025, a two-thirds decline and the lowest annual figure in over two decades, per NDSU Agricultural Trade Monitor analysis. NDSU estimated the annualized China-specific agricultural export shortfall at $14.9 billion — 41% larger than the $10.6 billion shortfall during the 2018–2019 trade war. Soybeans accounted for $6.8 billion of the loss; beef and cotton each contributed $1.3 billion; corn $333 million; and tree nuts $964 million. For the first time in more than 20 years, Chinese importers purchased no soybeans from the U.S. autumn 2025 harvest, forcing American farmers to store their crops as prices fell to a five-year low. Brazil's soybean exports to China hit record levels in 2025, topping 85 million metric tons — an 18% increase — as U.S. market share evaporated.

original_assignment_row.description_short: SEC Drops 60%+ of Crypto Enforcement Cases in Mass Regulatory Capitulation
original_assignment_row.description_medium: The supplied summary attributes to a December 2025 New York Times investigation a finding that the SEC eased up on more than 60% of crypto cases open at the start of Trump’s second term. It names several cases and alleged political connections, but the linked article could not be retrieved in the focused source review. The sample, case statuses, and causal claims need confirmation.
original_assignment_row.description_long: Within weeks of Trump's inauguration, the Securities and Exchange Commission under acting chair Mark Uyeda began systematically dropping enforcement actions against the crypto industry, which had spent more than $100 million supporting Trump's election. By February 21, 2025, the SEC dismissed its nearly two-year case against Coinbase, the largest U.S. crypto exchange, which had been charged with operating as an unregistered securities exchange. On March 20, 2025, the SEC dropped its four-year case against Ripple Labs and its XRP token. The agency also dropped or froze cases against Kraken, Gemini, Binance, and Robinhood. A December 2025 New York Times investigation found that the SEC had eased up on more than 60% of the crypto cases that were in progress at the start of Trump's second term — a retreat from a single industry with no legal precedent. The investigation into Justin Sun, who had invested $45 million in Trump's World Liberty Financial, was settled in March 2025 for $10 million with no admission of wrongdoing, after being paused following his WLF investment. Senator Elizabeth Warren demanded explanations for the apparent connection between Sun's investment in the Trump family business and the SEC's decision to drop its case against him. The mass regulatory pullback directly enriched the crypto industry that had funded Trump's election while benefiting the Trump family, which held billions in crypto assets subject to SEC oversight.
